purpose: Protect early play while restoring the full adult historical comparison baseline.

mortality.description: Only ages below 18 retain discounted comparison bands: age 0 uses 6%, ages 1-4 use 3%, and ages 5-17 use 6%. From completed age 18, the baseline uses 100% of the converted Roman Egyptian female comparison probability. In causal-health play, adult bands calibrate serious illness episodes; Health, care, household support and dangerous choices can change an individual's outcome. Childhood keeps its existing causal-health rules, so the discounted childhood bands are reference settings rather than a promised observed survival rate.

notes: The original mortality-model.json and legacy game-balance.json remain unchanged.
Age 18 is a gameplay boundary for this adjustment, not a claim about a universal ancient adulthood threshold.
Exact Ptolemaic Alexandrian rates are unavailable. The later Roman Egyptian female model is a disclosed comparison.
Calibrated neutral reference: Health 50, care 0.55, no household support. Adult severe-episode incidence times case fatality equals the unreduced annual comparison probability.
Illness selection, severity, Health and care responses are authored mechanics, not measured ancient cause-specific or treatment probabilities.
Source life expectancy at birth does not describe a cohort with protected childhood or an individual player's expected death age.
The 95+ annual tail remains an assumption derived from remaining life expectancy. Age 100 completes the record and does not itself cause death.
